Ranked by Welch's t-test p-value (potato-spiker = group of 9 subjects whose glycemic response to potatoes is disproportionately higher than to grapes; grape-spiker = group of 6 subjects with the opposite pattern):

LIPID SPECIES MEDIATION ANALYSIS

Three lipid-class metabolites among the top 10 were tested for mediation of insulin resistance (SSPG, HOMA-IR) and beta-cell function (DI) via the Baron & Kenny framework with Sobel test:

1. L-Palmitoylcarnitine (C16:0 AC) — a long-chain acylcarnitine marking incomplete mitochondrial beta-oxidation. Estimated 61% mediation of group→DI (beta-cell function) effect. Sobel p = 0.49 (not significant).

2. Hydroxybutyrylcarnitine (C4:0,OH AC) — a short-chain hydroxy-acylcarnitine reflecting incomplete fatty acid oxidation. Estimated 95% mediation of group→DI effect. Sobel p = 0.39 (not significant).

3. 3beta,16alpha-Dihydroxyandrostenone 3-sulfate — an androgenic steroid sulfate ~2.4× higher in potato-spikers. Showed suppression rather than mediation (negative proportion mediated for DI).

None of the three lipid species reached statistical significance in the Sobel test for any outcome (all p > 0.05). However, both acylcarnitines showed large proportion-mediated effect sizes (61-95%) for beta-cell function (DI), consistent with the known role of acylcarnitines as biomarkers of mitochondrial lipid overload and insulin resistance. The small sample size (n=13-15) limits statistical power for mediation testing. The gamma-glutamyl dipeptide (rank 2) showed a suggestive mediation trend for HOMA-IR (Sobel p = 0.066).

**Spiker group classification**: Computed from CGM iAUC z-scores per food. Potato-spikers (n=9 with metabolomics data) are subjects whose potato glycemic response is >0.5 SD higher than their grape response; grape-spikers (n=6) show the opposite pattern. Potato-spikers have significantly worse insulin resistance (SSPG: 176 vs 85 mg/dL; HOMA-IR: 2.91 vs 1.45; fasting insulin: 11.8 vs 6.5 uIU/mL) and lower beta-cell function (DI: 1.48 vs 1.92).

**Top 10 differentially abundant metabolites**: The most discriminating metabolites include three acylcarnitine/steroid lipid species (palmitoylcarnitine, hydroxybutyrylcarnitine, dihydroxyandrostenone sulfate) consistently elevated in potato-spikers, alongside gamma-glutamyl dipeptides and monoacylglycerol. Grape-spikers show higher catechol sulfate and a drug metabolite.

**Mediation results**: None of the Sobel tests reached p < 0.05 due to limited sample size (n=13-15). However, both acylcarnitines showed large proportion-mediated estimates for beta-cell function (61-95%), consistent with the known role of acylcarnitines as biomarkers of mitochondrial lipid overload driving insulin resistance and beta-cell dysfunction.
